faq.q: How do warehouse robots know where they are?
faq.a: Many read square codes stuck on the floor in a grid, using a camera underneath. Wheel sensors fill in between the codes, so they always know their spot.

faq.q: How do warehouse robots avoid crashing?
faq.a: A central computer plans every robot's route and reserves squares of the grid so two robots never aim for the same spot at once. Robots also have sensors to stop if something is in the way.
asks: Do warehouse robots crash into each other?

faq.a: Walking to fetch items takes up much of a picker's time. Bringing shelves to workers speeds up orders, cuts walking, and lets shelves be packed closer together.

faq.q: How much can a warehouse robot lift?
faq.a: It depends on the model, but some of Amazon's shelf-carrying robots can lift loads of several hundred kilograms.

faq.q: Why do popular items end up near the packing stations?
faq.a: The system tracks what sells often and returns those shelves to spots closer to the workers, so the next trip is shorter.
asks: How does a warehouse decide where shelves go?

facts: Amazon bought Kiva Systems, maker of shelf-carrying warehouse robots, in 2012.
Amazon reported having more than 750,000 mobile robots in its operations in 2023.
